description.p: Rusty Inbox is an open-source desktop mail client for IMAP and SMTP accounts: Gmail (with an app password), Fastmail, iCloud, Yahoo, cPanel and any other standard mail server. The mail engine is native Rust and the interface is Qt Quick, so the window starts quickly and stays light on memory.
Your mail is stored locally on your computer. There is no account with the developer, no cloud service in between and no telemetry.

ul.li: Smart Inbox: mail from people first, with notifications and newsletters grouped separately
All accounts in one unified inbox
Compose, reply, reply all and forward with a rich-text editor
Undo Send and Send Later
Templates for the replies you write every week
Drafts that sync with your mail provider
Done, Snooze, Pin and bulk actions, each with undo
Keyboard shortcuts for every action
Follows your desktop theme and font
Import of accounts from Thunderbird

screenshot.caption: Smart Inbox groups mail from people, notifications and newsletters

description.p: Push that stays connected, and fewer connections to your mail server:

ul.li: Accounts with push no longer log in for a full check every minute; their other folders are checked every 10 minutes
New mail and pushed updates reuse the push connection, so the app holds one connection per account
A push connection that a firewall cut silently is noticed within about two minutes and reopened
New mail shows the moment it arrives (IMAP IDLE push), with a regular check for servers without it
Download attachments of received mail: open one with a click, save it anywhere, or save all of a message's attachments at once
Click any name or address in a message (From, To, Cc, Bcc) to open the person's card: write to them, copy the address, or see all your conversations with them
A reply to a conversation marked Done or snoozed brings it back to the Inbox (it stayed hidden)
Attachments of large messages show once the message is opened

description.p: In-app updates and a reader fix:

ul.li: Settings → Updates: check for new versions daily, weekly or on demand, read what changed, and install with one click (AppImage, Linux binary, Windows, macOS)
Optional automatic installs in the background for AppImage and Linux binary installs
Messages already downloaded open at once, even while mail is syncing
Mail sync no longer stalls when a server stops answering; accounts on one server connect one after another
One stuck account no longer stops the others from syncing
Opening the app from a shortcut or launcher brings its window to the front, also from the tray
Logs are written to a file for troubleshooting
